nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many climatic zones does the Code for Thermal Design of Civil Buildings in China indicate?
nodes.answer: The Code indicates five climatic zones: severe cold areas, cold regions, hot summer and cold winter regions, mild regions, and hot summer and warm winter regions.
nodes.paragraph: As a unique geographical unit in China, the Sichuan Plateau can exchange and share its research and practical experience in energy efficiency improvement with similar regions in the world. Methodology and material As shown in Fig. 1, the research method mainly uses field measurements, questionnaire surveys, and energy simulations to conduct an in-depth analysis of the factors affecting the energy consumption of residential buildings in Sichuan Plateau, and to measure and quantitatively analyse the indoor thermal environment of local traditional residential buildings. The key factors of high energy consumption are identified, and some energy- saving improvement and optimization measures and economic suitability analysis are proposed. Research object The Sichuan Plateau region is composed of three prefectures: Garze Prefecture, Aba Prefecture, and Liangshan Prefecture, as shown in Fig. 2, Aba is located in the Sichuan Plateau region, about 104.27 least longitude, 30.35 latitude, the highest altitude in the territory is about 6250 m, and the average altitude is 3500 4000 m. According to the Code for Thermal Design of Civil Buildings, there are five climatic zones in China, namely severe cold areas, cold regions, hot summer and cold winter regions, mild regions, and hot summer and warm winter regions30.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What major initiative is driving the need for new building regulations according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP) presented by the Spanish Government in October 2020 is a fundamental driving force behind the new building regulations.
nodes.paragraph: Also, the NECP envisages the need for higher taxes on heavily polluting activities. The Technical Building Code laysdown new building regulations, to ensure that domestic energy consumption is low. A fundamental driving force behind many of these initiatives will be the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP), presented by the Spanish Government inOctober 2020, which proposes assigning 39% of the funds that Spain receives under the Next Generation EU (NGEU) programme to the green transition; see Cansino et al. (2016) for a description of the policy measures to control carbon emissions in Spain. Ensuring that energy policies are as effective as possible requires an understanding of the main dynamics and drivers of emissions. Within this context, the interest in modelling and forecasting GHG emissions is without doubt. Carbon dioxide (CO 2) emissions, largely by-products of energy consumption, account for the largest share of GHG and, consequently, the analysis of GHG emissions has usually focused on CO 2 emissions; see, for instance, Friedlingstein et al. ( 2022 ), who describes the Global Carbon Project that produces world-wide projections of CO 2emissions in preparing the annual Global Carbon Budget, which is considered in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPPC) reports.

nodes.question: What climatic zones are referenced in the context of the Sichuan Plateau?
nodes.answer: The climatic zones referenced are severe cold areas, cold regions, hot summer and cold winter regions, mild regions, and hot summer and warm winter regions according to the Code for Thermal Design of Civil Buildings.
